text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- The Swiss Israeli Community (SIG) said in a press release that it wanted profits from Nazi gold and unclaimed funds of Holocaust victims held at the Swiss National Bank to be used for humanitarian purposes and for research.
- Switzerland's depressed beef market, due to the BSE, or "mad cow" epidemic, is not likely not recover next year the World Trade Organisation said.

- The Swiss machine industry continues to suffer from recession. Orders from abroad dropped, for the first time in five years, by 7.7 percent in the first nine months of 1996. - Sika Group's nine-month profit rose to 1.05 billion Swiss francs in 1996, compared to 1.02 billion in the same period of 1995.
- Rhone-Poulenc Filtec AG will cut another 55 jobs in 1997 due to the low demand for chemical fibres.
- Security technology group Kaba posted a 16 percent profit rise to 14 million Swiss francs for the 1995/96 fiscal year ended in June.
- The Swiss Cartel Commission wants rental prices of skis, snowboards and sleds to be lowered and has ordered dealers of sports items to stop implementing previous standard prices.
- Some 80 tonnes of antibiotics are fed to animals in Switzerland annually, according to the Swiss Animal Protection Agency.
